parsed.why: Sexuality ban upheld in 2024 with thin enforcement data. Trans-specific record includes a teen assaulted then charged with fraud for presenting as a woman, and no SOGI protections or recourse. Structural signals point toward high risk.

Public same-sex affection is criminal, with a domestic report of false-accusation arrests and police torture of LGBTQ people. No SOGI protections, no legal gender recognition, and taboo framing. Trans-specific data is absent, so structural signals drive the rating.

Recognition is closed and a 2024 education law bans gender-identity content, which is state threat-framing. Survey data shows 46% avoid locations from fear of assault. Hate-crime enforcement fails, though anti-discrimination coverage and some court wins partly offset this.

Courts protect gender identity, transphobia is criminalised, X markers exist and bathroom guidance is affirmative. Main exposure is that trans women arrested may be held in masculine units in one state's system, plus violence and robbery risks. Overall reduced risk.

Decriminalised since 2010 with a constitutional SOGI ban, but no gender-marker route, conservative mores, and reporting discouraged by police distrust. One unresolved 2018 trans killing and a flagged contradiction on the legal status add uncertainty.
